question: nj-founder-resources
summary: A founder in Milltown can get genuinely free, one-on-one help from three separate state/federal channels: the NJ Small Business Development Center (nearly all services at no cost, but an eRFC form is mandatory first), SCORE (free, confidential mentoring; Middlesex is listed under both Central Jersey and Princeton chapters), and the NJ Business Action Center helpline/live chat. Forming an NJ LLC costs $100 with the Division of Revenue plus a $75 annual report due by the last day of the formation month; EIN and NJ tax registration carry no state fee. Most NJEDA money is currently shut or mismatched: the Main Street Micro Business Loan is fully subscribed and closed, the Small Business Improvement Grant excludes home-based businesses, the Small Business Fund needs a full year of operation and fixed assets, and NJ Accelerate requires two full-time founders. For an AI-services founder the tech-specific options are the NJ AI Hub accelerator in West Windsor (no equity, free space during a 10-12 week cohort) and TechUnited's free individual membership; the SBA-backed NJRIC accelerator is free but requires 2+ employees and over $500k revenue, so it is out of reach at launch. Local paid options are modest: about $175/month for weekday coworking in North Brunswick, and chamber dues are quoted on request rather than published.

findings.finding: The NJ Small Business Development Center gives nearly all of its counseling and training at no cost, but no one gets a session until they file the electronic Request for Counseling (eRFC) form.
findings.evidence: "Nearly all of our services are provided at no cost through funding from federal, state, and local grants"; the About page also states "All clients must complete an eRFC (electronic Request for Counseling) form before receiving any consulting services." Services listed include company formation, business plans, raising capital, cash-flow management, certifications, accounting/tax, marketing and sales. Network described as 100+ staff and consultants with seven regional centers hosted at colleges/universities.

findings.finding: For Middlesex County the NJSBDC page that names the county is the Rutgers-New Brunswick center, which currently runs virtual-only appointments from a phone/email desk, not a walk-in office.
findings.evidence: Page headed "NJSBDC at Rutgers University- New Brunswick" with "(Serving Middlesex County)"; it says "Our Middlesex office is currently not offering in-person appointments" and that counseling/training "remain fully operational and available virtually"; contact is (609) 789-8364 / rutgersnb@njsbdc.com, hours Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30; the Location field reads "TBD" and the Regional Director is listed as "TBD."

findings.finding: The state's own business-support page confirms SCORE counseling is free and confidential, and lists two SCORE chapters that both claim Middlesex County.
findings.evidence: Business.NJ.gov: "SCORE is a national non-profit organization... They provide free, confidential, and professional business counseling"; its chapter list shows "Central Jersey Score: Somerset, Hunterdon, and Middlesex Counties" (centraljersey.score.org) and "Princeton Score: Middlesex, Mercer, Burlington, Camden, Gloucester & Salem Counties" (princeton.score.org). The same page says the NJ Business Action Center helps "all at no cost and strictly confidential" and that NJSBDC help is "free, hands-on guidance."

findings.finding: The NJ Business Action Center is a free, confidential navigation service with a live helpline and chat, useful for permit, registration and agency questions before spending money on advisers.
findings.evidence: NJBAC site publishes "Call Our Business Helpline 1-800-Jersey-7 (1-800-537-7397)", an option to "Request a Meeting With Us", and points to Business.NJ.gov live chat to "connect with NJBAC experts in real time"; it also offers a downloadable NJ Small Business Manual and referral services for mentors/online presence.

findings.finding: An NJ LLC costs $100 to form and $75 per year to keep alive; the fee schedule and the state's filing guide agree on both numbers.
findings.evidence: Division of Revenue fee schedule: LLC "Certificate of formation $100.00"; LLC "Annual Report $75.00" (also $75 for corporations and LPs; $30 for non-profits). Business.NJ.gov: "Every business in NJ must file an annual report... submitting a $75 filing fee," due "every year on the last day of the month, in the month in which you completed your business formation," and failure to file "can result in the revocation of your business."

findings.finding: The federal EIN and the state tax/employer registration (NJ-REG) are steps in the same checklist and no state fee is stated for either; the registered agent can be the owner as long as they have a New Jersey address.
findings.evidence: Business.NJ.gov registration guide: "All businesses should obtain an EIN" (online application "no more than 15 minutes," EIN issued immediately; fax ~4 days; mail 2-4 weeks per the page) and "All businesses must register for state taxes" with DORES, after which you receive an NJ Tax ID and, only if collecting sales tax, a Certificate of Authorization to Collect Sales Tax. Registered agent guidance: "This can be the business owner or someone else, but they need to have a New Jersey address." No fee is listed for NJ-REG on the page.

findings.finding: NJEDA's flagship micro-loan for very small businesses is closed to new applications right now.
findings.evidence: Main Street Micro Business Loan page banner: "Based on the significant number of applications already received, funding for the Main Street Micro Business Loan is fully subscribed... the NJEDA is no longer accepting new applications." The product itself was up to $50,000, 10-year term, 2% interest, no payments in year one, $100 application fee and $400 closing fee, for businesses formed at least six months, 10 or fewer FTEs and under $1.5M revenue.

findings.finding: NJEDA's Small Business Fund is a loan, not a grant, and its terms exclude exactly the businesses a new side venture is likely to be: home-based and less than a year old.
findings.evidence: Up to $500,000; eligibility requires being "in operation for at least one full year from date of application", no more than $3 million in total revenue, ability to "provide fixed assets (e.g. real property and machinery/equipment)", and states "Homebased businesses are ineligible." Fees: $300 application fee, guarantee fee up to 0.5%, closing fee 0.5%, commitment fee 0.5%, all non-refundable.

findings.finding: The Small Business Improvement Grant (50% reimbursement up to $50,000) is still described as rolling, but it requires a rented or owned facility and explicitly excludes home-based businesses.
findings.evidence: "Reimbursement of up to 50% of total project costs incurred up to $50,000"; project cost minimum $5,000; applicants must "Rent or own and operate from facility"; "Home-based businesses are not eligible for reimbursement for renovation or improvement projects"; applicants must certify wages of the greater of $15/hour or 120% of minimum wage; $100 approval fee; "Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until funding is exhausted."

findings.finding: NJEDA's NJ Accelerate money is gated behind founder time commitments that a side business cannot meet.
findings.evidence: To qualify, a company needs, within six months of graduating an Approved Accelerator: an NJ tax clearance certificate, "At least 50% of the company workforce works or pay taxes in NJ", "A minimum of 2 founders/ C-suites devoting 100% of their professional time to the Company in NJ and 80% of their time in New Jersey", and must be in a NJEDA targeted industry (which includes "Information and High Technology"). The program also lists an application fee of $500 for the investment benefit.

findings.finding: The most relevant AI-specific accelerator is the NJ AI Hub in West Windsor, run with Plug and Play: no equity taken, free workspace during the cohort, cohorts each year, and companies need to be at MVP stage.
findings.evidence: Reporting on the program: companies "from MVP and onward (venture-backed, but no publicly traded companies) are eligible"; Plug and Play "will run selected cohorts... for 10-12 weeks each year"; "Space is provided for free during the program. Afterward, companies can apply for paid space at the coworking site, pending availability"; "There is no equity taken... There is no direct funding tied to participation." The Hub itself is a 6,500-square-foot facility in West Windsor founded by Princeton University, the State of New Jersey, Microsoft and CoreWeave, and will house an entrepreneur co-working space and workshops.

findings.finding: The SBA-funded NJRIC 'free AI accelerator' looks ideal on price but its entry bar (2+ employees, >$500k revenue) rules out a pre-revenue consultancy.
findings.evidence: "a free AI, cybersecurity, and tech accelerator backed by the SBA"; to qualify a small business must "Be registered and operating in New Jersey," "Be an AI, Cybersecurity, IT, or other tech-related business," "Have two or more employees," and "Have revenues greater than $500k." Deliverables include coaching/mentoring and a cybersecurity/business-resilience assessment via Kean University's Center for Cybersecurity.

findings.finding: TechUnited:NJ charges founders nothing for individual membership and runs recurring free-format AI events, while company memberships start at $3,000 a year.
findings.evidence: Membership page: "Founders, entrepreneurs, students and individuals join free"; the free "Builder" tier includes member dinners and investor roundtables, "Ship & Run weekly. AI Demo Night monthly," preferred pitching consideration at AI Demo Night, and a weekly newsletter. Paid "Innovator" tier: "$3,000 under 50 staff, $6,000 to 250, $9,000 above."

findings.finding: Coworking within a few miles of Milltown is cheap by the month and very cheap by the day, so a paid desk can be treated as a variable cost.
findings.evidence: The CoWorking Space, North Brunswick published rates: "Daily Drop in - $35/day", "10 Daily Drop-ins - $140", "Weekday Co-Working - $175/month", "24/7 Co-Working (Non-Dedicated) - $250/month", "24/7 Co-Working Private Desk Cubicle - $350/month", "Virtual Mail starts at $25/month"; includes free parking, printing, up to 10 conference-room hours monthly.

findings.finding: Market research that would otherwise cost money is free with a New Jersey library card, and the state points to specific databases for competitor and prospect lists.
findings.evidence: Business.NJ.gov's business-support page lists, via the NJ State Library: Business Source Premier ("Over 2,300 full-text journals, including more than 1,100 peer-reviewed titles"), Regional Business News ("75 business journals, newspapers, and newswires"), and Reference Solutions ("7 Reference USA databases" including U.S. Businesses and U.S. New Businesses), describing them as "available for all New Jersey residents with a library card."

findings.finding: If borrowed money is ever needed, a nonprofit microlender will take a business under two years old, at a published fixed rate, with a 10% down payment.
findings.evidence: UCEDC: "fixed-rate (between 5.0% - 7.75%) up to six-year loans with as little as 10% down for start-up and existing businesses in New Jersey"; "Businesses in operation for less than two years can borrow a maximum of $35,000"; no prepayment penalties; eligible uses include equipment, fixtures, inventory, working capital, and renovations to owned commercial real estate that houses the business.

resources.name: NJSBDC Request for Counseling (eRFC) — Middlesex via Rutgers-New Brunswick center
resources.what_it_offers: Free one-on-one consulting and workshops on formation, business plans, capital access, cash flow, certifications, tax and marketing; Middlesex appointments currently virtual.
resources.cost: Nearly all services at no cost
resources.how_to_use_it: Submit the online eRFC first (mandatory for every client), then call (609) 789-8364 or email rutgersnb@njsbdc.com to schedule; describe the AI-agent pilot offer and ask for pricing and contract review help.

resources.name: SCORE Central Jersey / SCORE Princeton (free mentoring)
resources.what_it_offers: Free, confidential mentoring plus workshops and webinars; Middlesex County appears in both chapters' coverage.
resources.cost: Free (state page describes counseling as free; individual workshop prices not verified)
resources.how_to_use_it: Use the chapter link from the state's business-support page to request a mentor; ask for someone with professional-services sales experience to pressure-test the pilot pricing.

resources.name: NJ Business Action Center (NJBAC) helpline and live chat
resources.what_it_offers: Free, confidential help getting answers from state agencies, referrals, and a downloadable NJ Small Business Manual; live chat on Business.NJ.gov.
resources.how_to_use_it: Call 1-800-537-7397 or use Business.NJ.gov live chat for permit, registration and 'who do I ask' questions before paying anyone.

resources.name: NJ Division of Revenue fee schedule (formation and annual report)
resources.what_it_offers: Authoritative list of state filing fees, including $100 LLC certificate of formation and $75 LLC annual report.
resources.how_to_use_it: Budget and verify fees here, then file through the state's registration flow; diarise the annual report for the last day of your formation month every year.

resources.name: Business.NJ.gov registration guide
resources.what_it_offers: Step-by-step checklist: name search, EIN, entity formation, NJ-REG tax/employer registration, plus links to the name-availability and registration portals.
resources.cost: No fee stated for the guide, EIN, or NJ-REG; entity filing fee applies separately
resources.how_to_use_it: Work top to bottom once; keep the Entity ID and NJ Tax ID for contracts, W-9s and client vendor onboarding.

resources.name: Business.NJ.gov funding list (80 programs)
resources.what_it_offers: List of state and agency programs with eligibility and benefits summarized per item, including NJEDA loans, vouchers and tax credits (opened through the NJ Ignite funding URL, which renders the full list).
resources.how_to_use_it: Filter for programs a one-person, home-based, pre-revenue business can actually meet; most entries require employees, revenue, or a facility.

resources.name: NJEDA Small Business Improvement Grant
resources.what_it_offers: Reimbursement of up to 50% of project costs up to $50,000 for interior/exterior improvements or new furniture, fixtures and equipment.
resources.cost: $100 approval fee; project must be at least $5,000
resources.how_to_use_it: Only relevant once you rent a commercial space (home-based excluded); keep invoices, confirm tax clearance, and apply rolling while funds last.

resources.name: NJ AI Hub Accelerator (West Windsor, powered by Plug and Play)
resources.what_it_offers: 10-12 week cohort with mentorship, corporate/university connections, pilot and investor exposure, free workspace during the program, no equity taken.
resources.cost: No equity and no fee stated on program reporting; paid coworking after the cohort, pending availability
resources.how_to_use_it: Apply with an MVP-stage AI product and a New Jersey angle; a working agent demo matters more than a deck. Confirm the current cohort deadline directly, since the program site blocked automated access.

resources.name: TechUnited:NJ — Builder membership
resources.what_it_offers: Free individual membership: member dinners and investor roundtables, weekly Ship & Run, monthly AI Demo Night with preferred pitching consideration, weekly NJ tech newsletter.
resources.how_to_use_it: Join free, attend AI Demo Night to meet people who already sell to NJ businesses, and use the pitching slot once there is a pilot case study.

resources.name: NJRIC (New Jersey Regional Innovation Cluster) accelerator
resources.what_it_offers: Free SBA-backed AI/cybersecurity/IT accelerator: coaching, mentoring, a Kean University cybersecurity resilience assessment, capital introductions.
resources.how_to_use_it: Not eligible at launch (needs 2+ employees and >$500k revenue) — revisit once the consultancy has staff and revenue; the free cybersecurity assessment is worth asking about earlier.

resources.name: The CoWorking Space, North Brunswick
resources.what_it_offers: Flexible coworking a few miles from Milltown: day passes, weekday or 24/7 memberships, private desks, conference rooms, virtual mail.
resources.cost: $35/day; $175/month weekday; $250/month 24/7; $350/month private desk cubicle; virtual mail from $25/month
resources.how_to_use_it: Buy a $35 day pass for client meetings instead of committing monthly; add virtual mail if a Milltown home address should not appear on proposals.

resources.name: NJ State Library business databases (via local library card)
resources.what_it_offers: Free access to Business Source Premier (2,300+ journals), Regional Business News (75 business publications), and Reference Solutions (U.S. Businesses / U.S. New Businesses) for prospect and competitor lists.
resources.cost: Free with a New Jersey library card
resources.how_to_use_it: Build a target list of Middlesex County law firms, contractors, property managers, agencies and food businesses with employee/revenue filters before cold outreach.

resources.name: UCEDC microloan program
resources.what_it_offers: Fixed-rate microloans up to $35,000 for businesses under two years old (up to $50,000 for established, profitable businesses), terms up to six years.
resources.cost: 5.0%-7.75% fixed; as little as 10% down; no prepayment penalty
resources.how_to_use_it: Use only for a defined revenue-producing purpose (e.g., hardware for a sensor pilot) and ask about SBA microloan technical assistance, not for covering ordinary living costs.

resources.name: Middlesex County Regional Chamber of Commerce
resources.what_it_offers: 700+ member businesses, networking programs and signature events, committees, newsletter/website advertising and event sponsorship, access to county officials.
resources.cost: Not published on public pages; dues schedule is only in an image-based 2024 application PDF (ask for a quote)
resources.how_to_use_it: Attend a public event first and ask about a home-based/first-year rate before joining; the member list is a prospect list for AI intake work.

recommendations_for_us: Inference: spend the first two weeks only on free channels — file the NJSBDC eRFC, request a SCORE mentor, and call the NJBAC helpline — because all three publish no-cost service, so the binding constraint is time, not money.

Inference: budget roughly $175 for state fees in year one ($100 LLC formation + $75 annual report) plus $0 for EIN and NJ-REG, and skip paid registered-agent services at the start since the owner can serve as agent with a New Jersey address.

Inference: form the LLC only when the first paid pilot is signed (or immediately, if a client's vendor onboarding requires an entity), then start the clock — several NJEDA products (six-month formation rule, one-year operating rule) are measured from that date, so forming early quietly builds eligibility.

Inference: treat NJEDA money as a year-two option, not a launch plan. The micro-loan is closed, the improvement grant excludes home-based businesses, the Small Business Fund demands a year of trading plus fixed assets, and NJ Accelerate needs two full-time founders — so do not write a plan that assumes a state grant.

Inference: pursue the NJ AI Hub accelerator as the single tech-specific bet, because it takes no equity, gives free space during the cohort, and explicitly wants MVP-stage companies; a working phone-intake agent demo for a law firm or contractor is the entry ticket.

Inference: join TechUnited free and use AI Demo Night and Ship & Run as the lowest-cost route to NJ business owners and investors, rather than paying $3,000 for a company membership before there is revenue.

Inference: buy coworking by the day ($35) for client meetings and skip monthly desks until a pilot pays for one, since a home-based consultancy's credibility comes from the demo and references, not the address.

Inference: use the NJ State Library databases to build a named list of 100-200 Middlesex County targets segmented by the five verticals, since free licensee data beats guessing and the state publishes the databases as free with a library card.

Inference: ask NJSBDC specifically for pricing, contract and scope-of-work help on the pilot/set-up/care-fee structure, because its published service list covers capital access, cash-flow and business planning — the areas where a technical founder is most likely to underprice risk.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming a state micro-grant will fund launch costs: NJEDA's Main Street Micro Business Loan page currently says funding is fully subscribed and it is no longer accepting applications, and its application fees are non-refundable.
Home-based exclusions: both the Small Business Improvement Grant and the Small Business Fund state that home-based businesses are ineligible, which rules out a founder working from a Milltown house.

Tech accelerators that look free often have revenue or headcount floors: NJRIC requires two or more employees and more than $500k in revenue, and NJ Accelerate requires two founders at 100% time in New Jersey.
Skipping the NJSBDC eRFC form: the state network states no consulting happens until that form is submitted, so time spent emailing counselors first is wasted.

Trusting the widely repeated $125 New Jersey LLC figure: the Division of Revenue schedule lists $100 for the LLC certificate of formation and $75 for the annual report, so budget from the fee schedule, not from blog posts.

Forgetting the annual report: it is due the last day of the formation month every year, the business is responsible even without a state notice, and missing it can revoke the entity — which would break client contracts.

Joining a chamber before testing it: dues are quoted rather than published, so paying up front for a one-person, home-based consultancy risks buying a member list you could have assembled free from library databases.

caveats: NJSBDC's own pages conflict on county coverage: the Request for Counseling page lists The College of New Jersey (TCNJ) as serving Middlesex, Hunterdon, Somerset and Mercer, while the Rutgers-New Brunswick center page says '(Serving Middlesex County)'. Confirm which center will take the case when filing the eRFC.

score.org, centraljersey.score.org, njaihub.org and middlesexcountynj.gov all returned HTTP 403 to our fetcher, so SCORE's free-counseling claim is sourced from Business.NJ.gov and the NJ AI Hub program details come from secondary reporting (a Plug and Play/NJ AI Hub announcement and a New Jersey tech newsletter), not from the accelerator page itself.

The NJ AI Hub accelerator's application deadlines were reported inconsistently (a January deadline for one batch, a July deadline for another); the program page could not be read directly, so treat any date as unconfirmed until checked on njaihub.org.

NJEDA program status changes quickly (the micro-loan closed, and grant pages are updated as funds are exhausted), so re-check each program page before relying on it, and note that all NJEDA application fees cited are non-refundable.
The NJEDA R&D voucher and clean-energy voucher items surfaced by the state funding list were not verified against their own program pages and are not included as findings.
data_gaps: Middlesex County Regional Chamber of Commerce dues: the only public schedule is an image-based 2024 membership application PDF that our tools could not read, so no dollar figure is reported here; the chamber's phone is 732-745-8090.

SCORE's sign-up mechanics (ZIP-based mentor request form, workshop prices, whether any Central Jersey workshops are paid) could not be verified because score.org blocked automated access; Business.NJ.gov only confirms that counseling is free.
Middlesex County's Office of Business Engagement page (county-level free business help) returned HTTP 403 and could not be reviewed, so its services are not listed.

NJ Ignite (coworking rent support of 2, 4 or 6 months) still displays on njeda.gov with no fees, but one secondary source said applications closed June 30, 2025; the closure could not be confirmed on an official page, so treat NJ Ignite as status-unknown.

No 2024-2026 survey or founder account with sample sizes on the dollar value of NJ small-business assistance was located within this research pass; the findings are program-documentary rather than outcome-measured.
NJSBDC's SBIR/STTR technology-commercialization page is visibly outdated (it promotes a 2019 road tour), so the depth of current tech-commercialization help for an AI services firm is unverified.
Milltown borough licensing/zoning for a home-based consultancy could not be verified: the municipal code pages (ecode360) returned HTTP 403, so no local permit cost or requirement is stated here.
